title: PoE 2 Mana and Spirit Problems: Fix Resource Sustain
summary: Why your skill loop stalls, your mana flask never keeps up, or an aura will not enable: mana cost versus recovery, Spirit as a reservation pool, supports that inflate cost, and how mapping and boss fights differ.
description: A diagnostic-first PoE 2 resource sustain guide: the relationship between mana cost, regen, leech, on-kill, flasks, and trigger rate; why Spirit is a separate reserved pool; how supports raise cost or reserve Spirit; why boss and mapping resource problems differ; alternative pools like Life and Energy Shield; and a 10-second loop method to find the break point.
prerequisites: You can cast your main skill but the loop stalls, or an aura will not turn on
You understand that mana is spent per cast while Spirit is reserved by persistent effects
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: PoE 2 Herald of Ice, a Spirit-reserving skill buff that illustrates the difference between spent mana and reserved Spirit

items.title: Why does my loop stall?
body: Your mana spent per cast exceeds what you recover between casts from regen, leech, on-kill, and flasks.
In boss fights without adds, on-kill and leech sources dry up, so the same setup that cleared maps runs out of mana.

items.title: Why won't my aura enable?
body: Spirit is a reserved pool, not spent mana. If your reserved Spirit exceeds your maximum, the persistent buff cannot activate.
Free Spirit from other reservations first, then re-enable the aura or support.

items.title: Fastest fix?
body: Record a 10-second cast loop: count casts, note mana spent versus recovered, and find where recovery fails.
Often the cheapest fix is removing a support that inflated the cost, not stacking more recovery.

sections.title: Mana vs Spirit: two different pools
paragraphs: Mana and Spirit solve different problems and are easy to confuse. Mana is spent every time you cast a skill. Spirit is reserved by persistent buffs, auras, and some supports, and is unavailable while reserved.
bullets: Mana: consumed per cast; recovered through regeneration, mana leech, on-kill mana gain, and flasks or charms.
Spirit: a pool reserved by persistent effects; if reserved exceeds maximum, the effect will not turn on.
A support can both raise a skill's mana cost and reserve Spirit for a persistent buff, hitting you twice.
Treat them separately: fixing mana never fixes a Spirit overflow, and vice versa.

sections.title: Pick your symptom
sections.intro: Start here. Choose the symptom that matches, then use the detailed diagnostic below to find the break point.

options.label: Mapping is fine, boss fights run dry
Aura or persistent buff won't enable

rules.title: Mapping fine, boss dry
steps: Your recovery leans on on-kill and leech, which need steady kills.
Bosses with long phases and no adds cut those sources off.
Add standing recovery (regen, a mana flask/charm) rather than only on-kill or leech.

rules.title: Aura will not enable
steps: Reserved Spirit is greater than your maximum Spirit.
Unsocket or lower other persistent buffs and supports to free Spirit.
Re-enable the aura once total reservation fits your pool.

rules.title: Triggered skills drop out
steps: Triggered skills still cost mana when they fire, on top of the trigger skill.
If trigger rate is high, total mana spent spikes between recoveries.
Lower trigger frequency or add recovery sized to the trigger rate, not just the main cast.

rules.title: Always out of mana
steps: Base mana cost exceeds base recovery in every context.
Record a 10-second loop to measure the exact gap.
Fix the largest single source first: usually a support that inflated cost or missing regen.

defaultResult.title: General first step
steps: Record a 10-second cast loop: casts, mana spent, mana recovered.
Identify whether recovery fails everywhere or only without kills.
Then open the detailed diagnostic to size each fix.

sections.title: Detailed diagnostic
sections.intro: Choose the resource you want to inspect. We show what raises its cost, what recovers it, and the check order.

rules.title: Mana cost vs regen
steps: Compare the skill's mana cost to your mana regeneration per second.
A support that adds mana cost can push cost above regen even if base cost was fine.
Fix order: remove cost-inflating supports, then add flat regen or -mana cost modifiers.

rules.title: Leech and on-kill
steps: Leech and on-kill mana only return while you are dealing damage and securing kills.
They are excellent in maps, weak in long boss phases with no adds.
Do not rely on them as your only recovery in boss-focused content.

rules.title: Flask and charm
steps: A mana flask or charm restores a burst on use and refills from charges.
Check charge gain: if you rarely take the actions that grant charges, recovery stalls.
Keep one reliable standing source even when flasks are on cooldown.

rules.title: Spirit reservation
steps: Sum every persistent buff and support reservation against your maximum Spirit.
If the sum exceeds maximum, the last effect will not enable.
Trim reservations before adding new auras or persistent supports.

rules.title: Alternative pools
steps: Some skills cost Life instead of mana; Energy Shield and Runic Ward are separate pools.
Verify the pressured pool directly: a Life-cost skill will not be fixed by mana regen.
Size recovery to whichever pool your skill actually spends.

defaultResult.title: General check
steps: Name the exact pool under pressure (mana, Spirit, Life, ES, Ward).
Measure spent versus recovered over a 10-second loop.
Address the largest gap first, then re-test in both mapping and boss contexts.

sections.title: Cost of each fix
sections.intro: Not every fix costs the same. Rank options from cheapest to most disruptive before you commit.

rows.detail: No refund needed; just remove the socket. Cheapest first step if a support raised mana cost or reserved Spirit you did not need.

rows.item: Add a mana flask or charm
rows.detail: A burst source on use. Cheap to obtain, but depends on charge gain and has cooldown.

rows.item: Swap gear for -mana cost or +mana regen
rows.detail: Look for reduced mana cost or increased mana regeneration on rings, amulet, or body armour. Cost depends on whether you craft or trade.

rows.item: Respec into mana or Spirit nodes
rows.detail: If you must path to resource passives, use the refund NPC; this costs gold and reallocates points you may need elsewhere.

rows.item: Switch to a Life-cost or different skill
rows.detail: Moving cost from mana to Life changes which pool is pressured and is rarely the cheapest option.

sections.note: Start with the free or low-cost options. Removing a support or adding a flask often resolves the gap without a respec.

sections.title: Why mapping and bossing differ
paragraphs: The same skill setup can feel perfect in maps and impossible in a boss arena. The difference is almost always your recovery sources, not your skill.
bullets: Maps: steady kills feed on-kill mana and leech, so recovery looks unlimited.
Bosses: long phases and no adds starve on-kill and leech, exposing a weak base regen.
Test recovery in a sustained boss-like scenario, not just while clearing packs.
If a fix only works while killing, it is not a boss-proof fix.

sections.title: Solutions that actually work
paragraphs: Target the largest gap measured in your 10-second loop. Usually one change closes most of it.
bullets: Remove or swap a support that inflated mana cost or reserved unneeded Spirit.
Add a standing recovery source (mana regen or a flask/charm) that does not depend on kills.
Free Spirit by trimming other persistent buffs before adding a new aura.
For trigger-heavy setups, size recovery to the trigger rate, not just the main cast.
Verify the pressured pool directly if your skill spends Life, Energy Shield, or Runic Ward.

sections.title: Methods that do not fix it
paragraphs: Players often stack the wrong thing. Skip these and measure the gap first.
bullets: Piling on more leech when the fight has no kills: leech needs damage dealt and kills to matter.
Adding mana regen to fix an aura that will not enable: that is a Spirit problem, not mana.
Assuming one universal mana threshold fits every build: recovery needs scale with your own cost and cast rate.
Ignoring trigger cost: triggered skills still spend mana when they fire.

sections.title: Community questions
sections.intro: Common resource-sustain questions from Reddit and video comments, with our read and a direct suggestion.

cards.title: Fine in maps, dry in boss
body: Problem: the loop only fails during long boss phases.
Evidence: recovery leans on on-kill and leech that need steady kills.
Suggestion: add standing regen or a flask; do not rely on kill-based recovery.

cards.title: Aura greyed out
body: Problem: a persistent buff will not turn on.
Evidence: reserved Spirit exceeds maximum Spirit.
Suggestion: free Spirit from other reservations, then re-enable.

cards.title: Flask never enough
body: Problem: a mana flask cannot keep up.
Evidence: charge gain is too slow, or cost spikes from a support.
Suggestion: check charges and remove cost-inflating supports before stacking flasks.

cards.title: Trigger eats mana
body: Problem: triggered skills drain mana fast.
Evidence: triggered skills cost mana on top of the trigger skill.
Suggestion: size recovery to the trigger rate, not just the main cast.

entries.description: A walkthrough of diagnosing mana and Spirit problems, separating spent mana from reserved Spirit, and fixing sustain without a full respec.
entries.takeaway: Measure a 10-second loop, free Spirit before adding auras, and remove cost-inflating supports before stacking recovery.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: Separate the pools first. A mana fix never resolves a Spirit problem, and most 'out of mana' cases are really a missing standing recovery.
bullets: Always dry: record a 10-second loop and remove the largest cost source first.
Boss only: add standing regen or a flask; stop relying on on-kill or leech.
Aura won't enable: sum Spirit reservations and trim until they fit.
Trigger dropout: size recovery to trigger rate, not just the main cast.
Wrong pool: confirm whether the skill spends mana, Life, ES, or Ward before fixing.
